pa_right_wall.blurb: The largest wall at Pike Run in the Southwestern Highlands, with eleven climbs on sandstone. Nearly all of it is short top-rope lines, plus a couple of trad routes and one boulder problem at the harder end. Grades start with beginner-level terrain and mostly sit between the low 5.x range and 5.8, with a single 5.10 at the top. The base has a small open flat area with makeshift benches and room to lay out gear, so it suits families, new climbers and anyone teaching top-rope basics. Anchors are bolted and easy to reach from above, but slings help keep the rope off the rock.

pa_black_angus_area.blurb: A small bouldering cluster on the west side of Haycock Mountain near Nockamixon in southeastern Pennsylvania, part of the Hangar 18 zone. Eleven problems sit on boulders right beside the trail, a short walk in from the parking lot. The range is wide for so few climbs: a couple of easy warm-ups, a solid middle of V2 to V4, then a handful of serious problems reaching V9. A good stop if you want a quick circuit with a few hard projects, and the easy route-finding of Hangar 18 makes it simple to locate.

pa_over_the_falls_area.blurb: The first cluster of climbable boulders you meet at Hangar 18 on Haycock Mountain, near Nockamixon in southeastern Pennsylvania. It lies on the right as you hike the Hangar 18 trail up from the lot, so the walk is short and little navigation is needed. Eleven boulder problems run mostly from VB to V4, with a good number of easy ones that suit beginners and warm-ups, and one standout test-piece at V9. Bring crash pads; this is a place for a short session rather than a big day out.

pa_colflesh_boulder.blurb: A large boulder at the Colflesh Area of Governor Dick Park, also known as Mount Gretna, in south-central Pennsylvania. It sits left of and downhill from where you enter the area. Eleven boulder problems cover a spread from beginner-friendly V0-minus up to one V5 that takes the central line of the main block; the bulk of the problems fall between V0 and V3. Most can be done with a single pad. A good fit for climbers building up through the easier grades who also want one hard classic to try.

pa_elephant_boulder.blurb: A small boulder spot on the left side of the Colflesh Area at Governor Dick Park (Mount Gretna) in south-central Pennsylvania, a short walk from the nature center. Of the eleven problems, almost all are very easy, from VB to V1, with only one hard line at V6. The climbing is not outstanding, but the rock quality is good and the zero-grade moves are enjoyable. The ground around the main boulder is flat and roomy, which makes it a natural choice for kids, true beginners and groups who want space to hang out between attempts.

pa_box_boulders.blurb: A group of boulders in the Shamu Area at Governor Dick Park (Mount Gretna), south-central Pennsylvania. They stand in the middle of a small field shared with the Bulge Area, a short way below the Shamu boulder itself. There are eleven problems with a broad range: a few easy V0 climbs, a middle of V3 to V5, a trio around V7, and one V11 for the strongest climbers. The surrounding Shamu Area is big and loosely laid out, and gets overgrown in summer and fall, so spring or early winter visits are friendlier.

pa_brain_the.blurb: A cluster of rock within Bauer Rock on South Mountain, in the Bethlehem and Allentown area of eastern Pennsylvania. Eleven climbs, almost all boulder problems plus one top-rope line on the vertical wall at the back of the cluster. Most boulder problems fall between VB and V3, with a pair of hard roof problems at V8, and the top-rope line is a hard 5.12. Some roofs are fully horizontal. The path in is easy to miss, and in leafy months the rocks are hard to spot from the main trail.
